name: smbclient-ng
desc: Fast and user friendly way to interact with SMB shares
why: A friendly SMB client, a door into the Windows file-sharing protocol that most developers never look through.

brief.what_it_is: smbclient-ng is a Python command-line client for SMB file shares, the protocol Windows uses for network file sharing. You point it at a host with -H, authenticate with a domain, user, and password, hash, AES key, or Kerberos, and get an interactive shell. From there you list shares, browse and tree-view remote directories, read files (cat, head, tail, bat), and get, put, mkdir, rm, or mount remote shares. It also has local-side commands (lls, lcd, lcat) and a sessions command. Output is text in the terminal, and downloaded files land in the local filesystem.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no explicit motivation. It presents the tool as a fast and user-friendly way to interact with SMB shares, which points at a nicer replacement for the stock smbclient-style workflow.
brief.how_it_works: It is a Python tool installed from PyPI as smbclientng. Launching it opens an interactive prompt where each feature is a named command, such as dir, use <sharename>, get [-r], or mount <remote_path> <local_mountpoint>. Non-interactive use is available through -C for a single command, -S for a startup script of commands, and -N for non-interactive mode. The README does not describe the underlying SMB library or internals.

commands_seen.context: Install from PyPI using pip as a Python module.
Install into an isolated environment with pipx.
Quick start: connect to a remote SMB server with domain, user, password, and host. The password is written literally on the command line.
Inside the prompt, select an SMB share to work in.
Inside the prompt, download a remote file, or a directory recursively with -r.
Inside the prompt, mount a remote share path at a local mount point.
Inside the prompt, show a tree view of remote directories.
Inside the prompt, manage SMB sessions.
Shown in the README usage section to print the help and banner when run from a source checkout.

brief.install_notes: Install with pip, pip3, or pipx using the package name smbclientng. The command is installed as smbclientng, and the package also exposes smbng according to the metadata. The README lists no other runtimes, accounts, or hardware. Authentication is optional in the sense that you can supply a password, NT hash (--hashes), AES key (--aes-key), or Kerberos (-k with --kdcHost). Kerberos needs a reachable KDC and a fully qualified hostname. Default SMB port is 445 and default timeout is 3s, both changeable with flags.
brief.standout: It is a friendlier, feature-rich SMB shell: colored output, pretty-printed file views (bat, bhead, btail), a tree view, a metadata and sizeof helper, and a mount command, all under one roof with support for hashes and Kerberos. The README also advertises a separate Go rewrite that it calls faster and cross-platform.
brief.status: Probably maintained, but the evidence is limited. The README shows release and PyPI version badges, and its usage banner reports v2.1.8. I did not see a last-commit date, release date, or changelog, and I did not follow the links to check them. The author's maintainer and tooling badges point to an active author, and the README points users to a newer Go successor project.
brief.caveats: The README says a Go rewrite exists at TheManticoreProject/smbclient-ng and calls it faster and cross-platform by default, so the Python version may be superseded for new use. The quick start example puts a password directly in the command line, which will likely end up in shell history. The README gives no license information in what I read. It does not mention platform limits, and the mount command's requirements are not described. The README mentions the tool is 'friendly' and for interacting with shares, but it does not say whether it is intended for security testing, so I did not infer that.
